pages.title: A claim being circulated
pages.instruction: Read for the facts and the different priorities
pages.author: Neighbourhood post · simulated source
pages.subject: Permanent closure?
paragraphs: A neighbourhood post says a familiar café is closing permanently. It links to a photograph of a sign but does not name anyone from the business or reproduce the complete notice. Several replies repeat the permanent-closure claim and add assumptions about the staff and the reasons. None of those additions has a source in the material provided.

The post may alert readers to a real change, but it does not establish the duration or scope of that change. A responsible summary should not inherit every confident statement in the replies. Before forwarding it, compare the full notice and identify which details the business itself has actually confirmed.

pages.title: The narrower notice
pages.instruction: Read for the facts and the different priorities
pages.author: Café notice · simulated source
pages.subject: Service during renovation
paragraphs: The café’s notice says the dining area will close for renovation. Delivery will continue while work is carried out. It asks customers to follow the café’s own updates for changes in service. The excerpt does not say that the business is permanently closing and does not make claims about staffing.

This is a simulated notice for source-comparison practice, not a report about a real business. It is more directly connected to the service decision than the neighbourhood replies, but that does not justify adding a reopening date or an explanation that is absent. The practical distinction is between a closed dining area and an entirely closed business.

pages.title: A cautious phrase is not a source
pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: This post says the café is closing permanently. Would you share it?
lines.audioText: This post says the café is closing permanently. Would you share it?
lines.translation: Esta postagem diz que o café vai fechar definitivamente. Você compartilharia?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Not as it stands. It doesn’t identify the source of that claim
lines.audioText: Not as it stands. It doesn’t identify the source of that claim.
lines.translation: Não desse jeito. Não identifica a fonte dessa afirmação

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: The café is said to be closing, then? That sounds more cautious
lines.audioText: The café is said to be closing, then? That sounds more cautious.
lines.translation: Então dizem que o café vai fechar? Parece mais cauteloso

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Grammatically, yes, but it still passes on the claim without telling us who said it
lines.audioText: Grammatically, yes, but it still passes on the claim without telling us who said it.
lines.translation: Gramaticalmente, sim, mas ainda repassa a alegação sem dizer quem falou

questions.prompt: Why doesn’t “is said to” solve the source problem?

pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: The official notice says the dining area will close for renovation while delivery continues

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: That confirms a temporary change in service, not the permanent end of the business

lines.speaker: Kim

lines.audioText: Does it give a reopening date?

lines.audioText: Not in this excerpt. We should check rather than turn an expectation into a date.
lines.translation: Não neste trecho. Devemos conferir em vez de transformar expectativa em data

pages.title: What would you share?
pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: So I could say, according to the café’s notice, the dining area is closing for renovation
lines.audioText: So I could say, according to the café’s notice, the dining area is closing for renovation.
lines.translation: Então posso dizer: segundo o aviso do café, o salão vai fechar para reforma

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Yes, and keep the delivery detail because it changes what readers need to do
lines.audioText: Yes, and keep the delivery detail because it changes what readers need to do.
lines.translation: Sim, e mantenha o detalhe das entregas porque muda o que o público precisa fazer

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: I’d also correct the permanent-closure claim if I’d already shared it

lines.text: Exactly. Cautious wording doesn’t remove the responsibility to check and correct

lines.translation: Exatamente. Uma formulação cautelosa não elimina a responsabilidade de verificar e corrigir

pages.title: No reopening date has been set
pages.instruction: Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. The source has clarified the café notice. The dining area is closing for renovation, and delivery will continue, but a reopening date has not been set. The earlier post’s claim of permanent closure is not supported by the official notice. Could you revise the update with that attribution intact? Please don’t replace the false certainty with a confident reopening date. If people need to plan a visit, the useful next step is to check the café’s own updates rather than repeat the same unverified post. We can explain what the notice confirms and what it leaves open without implying that every part of the original rumour has been investigated independently
pages.audioText: Hi, Ana. The source has clarified the café notice. The dining area is closing for renovation, and delivery will continue, but a reopening date has not been set.
